title: Global Trends 2010
notes: First edition. Limited publication February 1997; the public 'Revised Edition: November 1997' is the text captured (the February version is not public). Prepared with the Institute for National Strategic Studies (National Defense University). No named scenarios: the scope note says the intent 'was not to produce an extensive list of alternative scenarios', so the edition has projection entries only. The whole web text (scope note, global trends, regional sections, implications) was mined because it is short. Figures in the original (population, energy) are not captured. Read from the 2019 Wayback copy of the dni.gov page; dni.gov and archive.dni.gov return 403 to scripts. Horizon 2010 has passed.

entries.label: World population over 7 billion by 2010
entries.quote: Population will increase by 1.2 billion to over 7 billion by 2010. About 95% of this growth will be in developing countries.
entries.subject: world population
entries.note: The Emerging Global Trends: Population. Also: about 95 percent of growth in developing countries.

entries.label: About half of world population in cities
entries.quote: about half of the world's population will live in cities compared with one-third today.
entries.subject: urbanization
entries.note: The baseline 'one-third today' (1997) looks low against commonly cited UN estimates of roughly 45 percent urban for the mid-1990s (not checked in this capture). Recorded as printed.

entries.label: Haiti's population doubles in 20 years
entries.quote: Haiti's population, for example, is expected to double over the next 20 years.
entries.subject: Haiti
entries.note: 'Next 20 years' from 1997. Passive ('is expected'); source not named.

entries.label: Per capita income growth over 2 percent a year
entries.quote: We project real growth in per capita income of over 2 percent per year between now and 2010.
entries.subject: global economic growth
entries.metric: world real per capita income growth, annual average 1997-2010

entries.label: Food production keeps pace with demand
entries.quote: Indeed, food production is likely to keep pace with overall demand.
entries.subject: food security

entries.label: Genetic engineering fuels a fourth agricultural revolution
entries.quote: We anticipate genetic engineering fueling a fourth agricultural revolution by the end of this timespan.
entries.subject: agricultural biotechnology

entries.label: Added oil production equal to OPEC's 1997 output
entries.quote: By 2010 the world will require added production of petroleum on the order of what OPEC produces now.
entries.subject: oil market
entries.metric: additional world oil production needed vs 1997

entries.label: Renewables do not significantly reduce fossil fuel reliance
entries.quote: Improvements in the efficiency of solar cells and batteries will result in greater use of these and other renewable energy resources, but they are unlikely to significantly affect global reliance on fossil fuels during this time period.
entries.subject: energy transition

entries.label: No power matches US battlefield technology
entries.quote: no power will be able to match US battlefield technological capabilities during this time frame
entries.subject: US military

entries.label: European growth 2-3 percent a year at best
entries.quote: growth rates are projected at 2-3 percent per year at best
entries.subject: Europe

entries.label: Enlarged NATO the primary vehicle for coalitions
entries.quote: The likely course at least through 2010 will be an enlarged NATO serving as the primary vehicle for launching and sustaining "coalitions of the willing."
entries.subject: Europe

entries.label: Political changes in Iran and Iraq by 2010
entries.quote: where political changes will occur in both countries by 2010
entries.subject: Middle East
entries.note: Parenthetical about Iran and Iraq in the Europe section.

entries.label: Russia economically weak through 2010
entries.quote: We believe Russia will remain economically weak through 2010 and beyond.
entries.subject: Russia

entries.label: Russia too weak to project force beyond neighbors
entries.quote: As a result, Russia will remain too weak to project its military force beyond its close neighbors.
entries.subject: Russia

entries.label: China not the region's dominant military power
entries.quote: While China has the potential to become the region's dominant military power, it is beset by significant internal problems that in our judgment will preclude it from becoming so during this time frame.
entries.subject: China military

entries.label: China-Taiwan unresolved; low risk of war
entries.quote: We believe that, while the risk of war is low, the China-Taiwan issue is unlikely to be resolved during this time frame.
entries.subject: Taiwan

entries.label: North Korea transformed; tensions eliminated
entries.quote: The next 15 years will witness the transformation of North Korea and resulting elimination of military tensions on the peninsula.
entries.subject: North Korea

entries.label: Southeast Asian disputes do not escalate into warfare
entries.quote: we estimate that increasing trade between these countries and regional organizations such as ASEAN will keep any regional disputes from escalating into warfare.
entries.subject: South China Sea
entries.note: Context: overlapping claims to the Spratly Islands contested by China.

entries.label: Gulf oil producers fail to diversify
entries.quote: By 2010 OPEC will have been in existence for half a century. Yet, the oil-producing countries in the region will have failed in weaning their economies away from oil.
entries.subject: Middle East

entries.label: Saddam Husayn gone from Iraq
entries.quote: In Iraq, Saddam Husayn will be gone and the challenge will be to see whether a modern, secular successor government emerges that does not threaten its neighbors.
entries.subject: Iraq

entries.label: De facto Palestinian state by 2010
entries.quote: We anticipate a de facto--if not de jure--Palestinian State by 2010.
entries.subject: Israel-Palestine

entries.label: India a major economic power, regional military power
entries.quote: India will emerge as a major power economically, and remain a regional power militarily.
entries.subject: India

entries.label: India does not join CTBT or FMCT
entries.quote: Efforts to draw India into the Comprehensive Test Ban Treaty or Fissile Material Cut-Off Treaty will falter.
entries.subject: nuclear weapons

entries.label: Nigeria's problems unresolved for 15 years
entries.quote: Nigeria's economic mismanagement, corruption, and political instability will not be resolved over the next 15 years.
entries.subject: Nigeria

entries.label: South Africa a successful regional leader
entries.quote: South Africa probably will be a successful regional leader, able to use diplomatic, political, economic and military leverage to help underwrite order in southern Africa.
entries.subject: South Africa

entries.label: PRI loses dominance in Mexico
entries.quote: In Mexico political power will become more diffuse as the Institutional Revolutionary Party (PRI) loses its dominance and a multi-party system emerges.
entries.subject: Mexico

entries.label: No major Cuban reform while Castro in power
entries.quote: In Cuba, major political and economic reform is unlikely to occur so long as Castro remains in power
entries.subject: Cuba

entries.label: No global anti-Western threat emerges
entries.quote: In this time frame, no country, no ideology, and no movement will emerge on a global scale to threaten US interests or to build and sustain an anti-Western coalition.
entries.subject: US global role
